title: 1989 AHSME Problem 3
statement: A square is cut into three rectangles along two lines parallel to a side, as shown. If the perimeter of each of the three rectangles is \(24,\) then the area of the original square is

solutions.text:
Let the square have side \(s.\) Since every rectangle has length \(s\) and the same perimeter, their three widths are equal and are each \(\frac{s}{3}.\) Thus \[ 2\left(s+\frac{s}{3}\right)=24, \] so \(s=9\) and the square’s area is \(81.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Equal perimeters force the three rectangle widths to be equal
Express one rectangle’s perimeter using the square’s side length
